title: Laravel Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Return a greeting
examples.description: Route::get connects a URL to a function. Open GET /.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/", fn () => "Hello, Asha!");

examples.title: Send JSON data
examples.description: The response helper can make JSON. Open GET /book.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/book", fn () => response()->json(["title" => "Moon Trip", "pages" => 24]));

examples.title: Read a name in the path
examples.description: Curly braces mark a route input. Open GET /hello/Ravi.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/hello/{name}", fn (string $name) => response("Hi, " . $name . "!")->header("Content-Type", "text/plain"));

examples.title: Read a query value
examples.description: Laravel can give the route a Request object. GET /search?q=cat reads the query value.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/search", fn (Request $request) => response()->json(["term" => $request->query("q", "")]));

examples.title: Limit a route input
examples.description: whereNumber only matches numeric path text. Open GET /double/4.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/double/{n}", fn (string $n) => response()->json(["answer" => (int) $n * 2]))->whereNumber("n");

examples.title: Build a URL from a name
examples.description: name gives a route a reusable label. GET /link builds a relative URL to that named route.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/hello/{name}", fn (string $name) => $name)->name("hello");
Route::get("/link", fn () => route("hello", ["name" => "Asha"], false));

examples.title: Send a client to another page
examples.description: redirect makes an HTTP redirect. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/start", fn () => redirect("/hello"));
Route::get("/hello", fn () => "Welcome");

examples.title: Report a missing item
examples.description: A JSON response can include an error status. Open GET /missing.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/missing", fn () => response()->json(["error" => "Book not found"], 404));

examples.title: Set a cache rule
examples.description: The header method adds response metadata. GET /note has a no-store rule.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/note", fn () => response("Practice note")->header("Cache-Control", "no-store"));

examples.title: Filter a collection
examples.description: A collection wraps values with useful methods. GET /scores filters scores and resets their numeric keys.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/scores", fn () => response()->json(collect([4, 8, 9])->filter(fn ($n) => $n >= 7)->values()->all()));

examples.title: Transform a collection
examples.description: map makes a new value for every collection item. Open GET /double.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::get("/double", fn () => response()->json(collect([2, 3])->map(fn ($n) => $n * 2)->all()));

examples.title: Share a path prefix
examples.description: A route group can share a prefix. Open GET /api/books.
examples.code:
<?php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
Route::prefix("api")->group(function () {
 Route::get("books", fn () => response()->json(["Moon Trip"]));
});
